transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, yeah, thanks. Um, I'm here because... well, things have just gotten really out of hand lately, and I didn't really know who else to talk to about it. I work as a cashier, you know, just scanning items, bagging groceries, standing on my feet for eight or sometimes ten hours a day, dealing with all sorts of customers. It gets really draining. But the real problem is what happens after I clock out. 

By the time my shift ends, I just get into this headspace, and I've been doing this thing where I leave work and I go straight to get takeout, but I don't just get a normal dinner. I order... well, I order a massive amount of food. Like, an embarrassing amount. I'm talking about getting three or four burgers, multiple large orders of fries, a whole box of fried chicken, and then I'll add on desserts, too, like a couple of pies and a large milkshake. It's literally enough food to feed an entire family, and I always wonder if the people handing me the bags think I'm taking it home to a party or my wife and kids or something. But I'm not. I just... I'll park my car somewhere quiet, and I will sit there and eat almost all of it entirely by myself. Just me. And I make sure I finish it before I even go home, because I just couldn't bear the thought of anyone actually seeing me eat like that. I just sit there in the front seat, eating until it's gone, and it's just becoming this huge, exhausting routine...
How do you feel after you've finished eating all that food by yourself?

Honestly, it's... it's just the worst feeling in the world. Like, while I'm eating, I'm kind of zoned out, almost numb, you know? But the exact second I swallow that last bite—like the last sip of the milkshake or the last fry—it's like this horrible switch flips in my brain. I'll look over at the passenger seat, and there's just... trash everywhere. Greasy paper bags, crumpled up wrappers, empty cardboard boxes. And the smell of the food in the closed car, which seemed exactly like what I needed twenty minutes earlier, suddenly just makes me feel absolutely sick to my stomach. 

Physically, I feel terrible. My stomach gets so stretched and tight that I usually have to unbutton my work pants just to sit there behind the steering wheel without being in actual pain. I feel so heavy and sluggish, almost like I can't breathe right because I'm just so stuffed. 

But the physical part isn't even the worst of it. It's the... the mental part. The guilt just hits me like a freight train. I just sit there staring out the windshield at whatever dark parking lot I pulled into, thinking, "Why did I just do that? Why did I do it again?" I feel so incredibly disgusted with myself. Just completely pathetic. I mean, I'm a thirty-year-old man, hiding in a car after a shift at the register, stuffing my face with enough food for five people. I usually just sit there in the quiet for another twenty or thirty minutes because I'm too full and too depressed to even turn the key in the ignition. I just sit there beating myself up, dreading having to gather all the trash into one big bag and figure out which gas station dumpster to throw it in so no one at my apartment complex sees it in my own trash. It’s just this heavy, dark, shameful feeling that completely ruins the rest of my night, every single time.
Do you usually feel stressed, anxious, or upset before you go to get all that food?

You know, it's funny you ask that, because... I'm really not sure. I don't think I feel upset, exactly? Or even anxious. It's hard to explain. Like, you'd think I'd be crying or pulling my hair out or having a panic attack before doing something so extreme, but honestly, I haven't really noticed feeling anything like that. 

By the time I'm walking out the sliding glass doors of the grocery store, it's more like... I don't know, like I'm just on autopilot. I'm not usually sitting there stewing over a rude customer who yelled at me about an expired coupon, even though that kind of thing happens all the time. I mean, just last Tuesday I had this lady scream at me over fifty cents because the system wouldn't take her rewards card, and it took ten minutes to clear the register. You'd think that would make me anxious or stressed out, but when I actually leave to go get the food, my brain is just... blank. It's like a static TV channel. 

I just clock out, hand my till over to the shift manager, walk out to my car—it's an older Honda, the AC barely works, so it's usually stifling hot in there after sitting in the sun all day—and I just get in, turn the key, and my hands just sort of steer me toward the drive-thru. I don't feel this big wave of stress or sadness pushing me there. I just feel this... this pull. Like I just *have* to do it. 

So, I don't know. I really don't think I'm upset beforehand. Or... maybe I am and I just don't realize it because my mind gets so completely focused on planning what I'm going to order? Like, I'll be in the car trying to figure out the logistics, wondering if I should hit the burger place first or the fried chicken place first so the fries don't get cold before I park, and that takes up all my attention. I really don't know. What do you mean by stressed, anyway? Do you mean like my heart racing, or feeling overwhelmed? Because it's definitely not that. It's just... I just do it. It's like I'm a zombie or something, just going through the motions of this terrible routine without even thinking about how I actually feel.
Do you think you would still feel the need to eat like this if you weren't feeling overwhelmed or stressed about your work or daily life?

Well, that's the thing, right? Like I was just saying, I don't even really feel like I *am* stressed or overwhelmed when it happens. So, I mean, if you took away the work stress—like if I won the lottery tomorrow and never had to stand behind that register again, never had to scan another barcode or deal with another angry customer complaining about the price of eggs—would I still do it? 

Honestly... yeah. Yeah, I think I probably would. Because it doesn't feel like it's connected to a bad day at work, you know? Like, I've had good days at work. Days where my manager actually compliments me, or the shift goes by super fast, or I just feel generally okay. And I still walk out to the parking lot, get into my hot car, and drive straight to get the food. It's like... it's just what I do now. It's become this ingrained part of my evening, no matter what happened during the day. 

I don't know, it's hard to separate the food from the rest of my life because it's just so constant. Like, even on my days off—when I don't even go near the grocery store, when I'm just sitting in my apartment watching TV or playing video games and I have absolutely zero responsibilities—the urge still creeps up. I'll be sitting on my couch, perfectly relaxed, not a care in the world, and suddenly that same pull just grabs me. And the next thing I know, I'm putting my shoes on, grabbing my keys, and driving around town hitting up three different drive-thrus just so the cashiers don't judge me for ordering so much at one place. 

So, yeah, I don't think it's about being overwhelmed. I mean, maybe it started that way years ago, I can't even remember anymore, but now? Now it's just this monster that shows up whether I'm having the worst day of my life or the best day of my life. It really doesn't seem to care how I'm feeling. It just wants to be fed.
Do you feel like you have control over eating this large amount of food, or do you feel like you're compelled to do it?

Control? Man, I... I wish I had even an ounce of control. If I had control, I wouldn't be doing this, right? So it's definitely the second one. I am completely compelled. 

It's like... okay, let me try to walk you through exactly how it happens, because it's so weird to try and explain to someone who hasn't felt it. I'll be sitting there in the driver's seat, right? I've got all the bags next to me, and I finally take that very first bite. And the exact second I do... it feels like something inside me just completely clicks off. Like a breaker tripping in a fuse box. 

And the craziest part is, the rational part of my brain is still kind of awake somewhere in the background. I'll literally be sitting there, chewing, and I'll be actively telling myself, "Demetrius, stop. You don't need any more. You're going to feel terrible, just put the bag down." I'm having this whole desperate argument with myself in my own head. But my body just doesn't listen. It's like my hands don't even belong to me anymore. Even while I'm practically screaming at myself to stop, my hands just keep reaching for the next thing. And the next thing. 

I'll finish a burger and before I've even swallowed it, my fingers are already diving into the carton of fries or unwrapping something else. It's terrifying, honestly. It's like being a passenger in my own body. I'm just watching myself do it, watching my hands move back and forth from the greasy wrappers to my mouth, and I just can't hit the brakes no matter how hard I try. I mean, have you ever felt like that? Where you know exactly what you're doing is a terrible idea, but you just physically can't make yourself stop? Because that's what it is every single time. It's a total hijacking.
Do you think you would eat this large amount of food if you were in a different environment, like on vacation or at a friend's house?

Oh, man. No. No, absolutely not. I mean, not in front of them, anyway. That’s actually a huge part of the whole thing for me. If I was at a friend's house, sitting on their couch playing Xbox or whatever, I wouldn't just whip out four burgers and start going to town. I would never, ever let anyone see me do that. The thought of someone actually watching me eat like that... it makes my stomach drop. 

I hide it. I hide it all the time because I am just so incredibly ashamed of what I’m doing. That’s why I was saying earlier about the car—I almost always eat in the parking lot. I’ll find some dark corner of a strip mall parking lot where the streetlights are burnt out, just so no one walking by can look in my windows and see me stuffing my face. 

And if I do bring it home... well, I can't let my wife see. So I have this whole routine where I'll leave the bags out in my trunk, and I'll go inside and act totally normal. I'll ask her how her day was, maybe watch a show with her, and I just sit there waiting. Just waiting and waiting until she finally says she's tired and goes to bed. I'll even wait an extra twenty or thirty minutes after she closes the bedroom door, just listening to make sure her breathing changes and she's actually asleep, before I sneak back out to the car to get the food. 

And the cleanup... man, the cleanup is like a covert operation. I can't just toss the bags in the kitchen trash. If she woke up the next morning and saw all those wrappers, she'd know. So I take all the greasy bags, the cups, and especially the receipts—because if she sees a receipt for thirty dollars at a drive-thru for just me, she's going to ask questions—and I literally stuff them all the way down at the very bottom of the trash can. I'll dig under the coffee grounds and the dirty paper towels just to bury the evidence so she won't see how much I had. 

So, yeah, if I was on vacation with people, or at a buddy's place... I'd probably still feel the urge, but I'd have to find a way to sneak away and do it in secret. I just can't bear the thought of anyone knowing. It's too embarrassing. You know what I mean? Like, the shame is almost as heavy as the compulsion itself. I just spend so much energy trying to make sure nobody ever finds out.
